runs.report_summary: Fixed stale module-level region cache in tallyboard/records.py: _region_for now validates that the cached region is still the one registered for that code before reusing it, so register/unregister/temporary/plugin changes no longer leak across calls or tests. Also made regions.temporary restore the previously registered region (if any) instead of always unregistering. Verified with 200+ randomized-order test runs (0 failures).

Root cause was module-level region cache in tallyboard/records.py: _region_for remembered the last region code/region across parse_rows calls without checking whether the region registry had changed. When tests (or real usage) registered/unregistered a region code such as "ne", a stale cached Region could be returned instead of looking it up again, causing order-dependent failures. Fixed cache validity check to re-lookup and only reuse the cached region when regions.lookup(code) is still the same object. Verified with 300 randomized test runs (0 failures) plus the originally failing seed.

The flash sale was racy because `Shop.reserve`, `Shop.receive`, and the backorder-filling triggered by `receive` performed multi-step read-modify-write sequences on the tables (availability checks, stock increments, hold placement, queue updates) without mutual exclusion, even though each table method is only individually atomic. Interleaving between worker threads could oversell a SKU or lose a stock update.

Fixed by serializing each logical shop operation with a per-`Shop` reentrant lock (`threading.RLock`): `reserve`, `receive`, and `available` now acquire it, and backorder filling runs while `receive` holds it. This makes check-then-act and stock increments atomic across threads while avoiding deadlock with the event bus/backorder desk. Full suite passes (16/16) and 200 repeated runs of the flaky test all pass.

Root cause was unsynchronized compound operations on shared Shop state (availability check + hold placement, stock updates, and backorder filling) across worker threads, allowing lost updates and oversells. Added a reentrant per-Shop lock and made reserve/receive/available/on_stock_received execute atomically under it. Verified 1000 consecutive runs of test_flash_sale_settles_exactly pass and full suite passes.

Added a per-Shop reentrant lock serializing reserve/receive/available operations (and made backorder filling use shop.available), eliminating cross-table races in the memory stand-ins that caused overselling and missed fills.

The flash sale ran orders and deliveries concurrently on a shared Shop, but reserve()/receive() were not atomic across the stock/hold/backorder tables: available() was a TOCTOU read, receive() did a non-atomic read-modify-write on stock, and backorder filling raced with reservations, causing oversolds and duplicate holds. Serialized each Shop operation with a reentrant lock (Shop._lock) around checkout.reserve, receiving.receive, and Shop.available, so stock checks, holds, backorders, and event-driven filling can no longer interleave.
